Francis-Henri Graffard's gelding merits plenty of respect as the trainer looks to win this prestigious race two years on the bounce, but it is his Epsom conqueror, JAN BRUEGHEL, that gets the nod. Tipperary winner Chou Chou ought to be a factor on this ground. This is a new trip for Carrickfinn in a bid to grab an elusive victory. He can be given a chance on his runner-up berth over 1m at this venue in June.

selections.comment: Jarlath Fahey's WARAZAM is consistent and ran a very pleasing third on her seasonal reappearance at Navan. She is entitled to come on plenty from that first run for almost eight months. Roderick delivered over 1m at Naas on Wednesday evening and is scheduled to make a quick turnaround carrying the mandatory 7lb penalty. He has placed form over 1m1f and is likely to be on many shortlists. Numidia didn't run badly in fourth in a higher grade at Down Royal and is capable of popping up, while Obama Army and Famous Enough could get into contention.

selections.comment: This looks a good opportunity for CRYPTO FORCE to regain a winning bracket. You have to go back to 2022 for his two career victories but, since then, he has been extensively plying his trade in Group races. He was last seen finishing mid-division in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot. Sam Coen's 7lb claim comes into play on Cristal Clere, who is actually weighted to beat Crypto Force. He has finished runner-up in his last couple of races and has Listed-placed form in the book. Dawn Spirit could go well with her sights lowered, while Penzance won five times in Britain and could be a useful recruit for Shark Hanlon.

selections.comment: A whole host of lightly-raced fillies in opposition in a Gr 3 in which backers need to tread warily, with so many unknown factors to ponder. STAYA ran very well when fifth in the Queen Mary here in June before improving a fraction on that when winning a Sandown Listed race last time and, with 6f likely to be within range, George Scott's filly appeals most. Old rival (and Queen Mary second) Flowerhead may be next best ahead of the very well-bred Newmarket debut winner Dance To The Music. Fitzella and potential improver Bella Lyra may be the pick of the rest.

selections.comment: This is competitive, with a fair few to consider closely. The one to appeal most is ROYAL DRESS, whose best form - notably when winning a 9f Gr 3 at The Curragh last July - entitles her to have a very big say. Though the bare figures of her last-time-out win at Pontefract don't compare with that, the style of that impressive win suggested that she is capable of running to that Curragh form again, in which case she'll have good prospects. Progressive 3yo Cajole is next best ahead of the eased-in-grade Chantilly Lace, whose fifth placings in the 1000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes entitle her to plenty of respect at Gr 3 level now, for all that those two renewals were substandard by top-level standards. Jancis and Pina Sonata are others to consider too.

selections.comment: Though last year's winner (stall one) and 2021 (four) were drawn low, a higher draw has generally been preferable in recent runnings of this race. A chance is taken on FRESH refinding his best form back at Ascot, in which case this 8yo will have every chance of repeating his win in this in 2022 on such form as last season's good, close third in this race. Fresh ran well enough on last month's seasonal debut to raise hopes he'll be ready to run to his best with that outing behind him now. Aalto is 5lb well-in after his excellent second in the Bunbury Cup last time, while he followed last season's win in that same Newmarket handicap with a solid effort here (around 2l ninth after being hampered). Stall three is a slight concern but he has strong claims otherwise. Classic comes here well-in and in fine form and appeals most of the rest while Oliver Show and Billyjoh are others for the shortlist.

selections.comment: This may go to TEROOMM, for whom the ground was very possibly too fast in the Britannia Handicap here last time and who has good prospects on his previous win in the valuable Silver Bowl at Haydock in May. He picked up well to score there and, progressing nicely at the time of that win, could well still be open to further improvement back on a less quick surface than last time now. Fellow 3yo Fearnot came on again when a very good third in the Britannia last time and, lightly raced, is likely to step up a bit again now. He may be next best ahead of another progressive sort in the 4yo Bullet Point. Cosi Bello and Hawksbill are among others to consider closely.

selections.comment: A smaller field than usual and no 3yos either but still an absorbing clash, with all five Group 1 winners. JAN BRUEGHEL showed considerable tenacity to wrest victory away from the challenging Calandagan at Epsom last time and though the margin was narrow (and, as such, confidence here cannot be sky-high), the more progressive profile of Aidan O'Brien's still lightly-raced second-season 4yo swings the vote decisively in his favour. First-time cheekpieces may well help put a greater edge on him too. Calandagan has since won well in a Group 1 in France and, with little to find on the bare form and with a proven liking for this track, is next best ahead of the thoroughly admirable Rebel's Romance, who doesn't have very much to find and, as ever, is likely to give it his all.

selections.comment: Pretty ordinary fare for a high-profile card such as this. The 3yos may be the ones to concentrate on, with the older contingent looking rather exposed. TENABILITY took a step forward when winning well last time and with the profile of a horse likely to come on again handicapping now, may be the answer. Kuredu King was off the mark in first-time blinkers last time and, fairly weighted up 2lb and bred to be better than this mark (his full brother Tuscan was a good horse at 7f, with an official mark of 105 at his peak), may be next best. The maidens Criminal and Venezuelan may, in that order, be best of the rest.

selections.comment: An open finale where most of the field can be given a chance but in form mare GLAMOROUS BREEZE gets the narrow verdict. She has won 3 of her last 6 and did well to finish as close as she did over C&D last time having missed the break. At the other end of the weights Tropical Storm looks a big threat on his handicap debut off what looks a lenient mark based on his Listed win. He was outclassed at the top level here last time but can bounce back down in grade with the fast ground in his favour. Veteran Michaela's Boy returned to form over the winter with a couple of AW victories and has held her form in defeat since on turf. She should remain competitive and could gain the final place ahead of the consistent Aramram who continues to creep up the weights.

Suspended Sentence showed plenty on his debut despite getting an interrupted run. He's at least a couple of lengths better than that bare form and given normal improvement he won't be any push over. Blooming Legend shouldn't be good enough to beat those two, but has been relatively consistent in her three starts and may be just too good for The Resdev Scholar and claim third spot.

Arabian Cobra also has strong claims providing he settles.

He then went on to come 2nd at Yarmouth before going on to absolutely blitz up by 7 lengths over the 2-mile trip at Southwell in September of that year. He has not been seen since, which could be a concern; however, I'm pretty sure connections would have him firing on all cylinders for his return, as he was in very good form prior to his break off the track. On a career high mark of 83 now, he does have to handle the step down in trip; however, he has run well over this sort of trip previously. La Pulga always runs well in his races, and although he has yet to win this season, he did place off a slightly higher mark than this last year; therefore, he can run well and claim a 2nd place once again. And Fast Fred is another runner in this who has been in great form at present; he can continue that decent form with a nice 3rd place finish in a higher class of race than last time.

He could be good enough to land a place on debut for an in-form team.

The Scott Dixon horse can go well here and fill the places.

Three of his four wins have come on fast ground but he's run up to similar levels both tries on good to soft and William Haggas's gedling looks very dependable given he's not been beaten over 3.5l in all ten runs. He's got very solid claims. Jubilee Walk is very interesting having had a pipe-opener at Chester recently after a poor spelll in the middle-east. Before that he made giant strides last term, culminating in a class 3 h'cap here on decent ground and although the run at Chester needs to be built on a big run looks on the cards and he can go close. Ed Bethell's top-weight, who is admirably versatile ground-wise is just preferred. Of the rest it's a tight call between Kildare Legend, Albany and L'Eagle Aid, with the former most feared given the potential for another step forward having hit a career peak last time in a class 2 event. Albany has to prove she stays the trip and didn't make an inspiring return last time but should strip fitter and it could be worth giving her another chance to show she has the stamina for this trip

selections.comment: Drifts Away has just kept on progressing and is very tempting but a tough wide draw might just scupper his chances. He's reluctantly overlooked in the favour of a trio drawn more favourably. BILLYB gets the nod looking to be coming to the boil nicely. He was favourite for this last year but never landed a blow out wide and there was possibly something amiss as he trailed in 17th of 18. However, he's gone well at this track before and handles cut in the ground and can be given another chance off a 3lb lower mark than for this last year. Bellarchi is a serious danger arriving in such good form and she's rated higher in the past and is perhaps rediscovering those former levels. Ata Rangi needs excusing his latest effort but that was a first blip in an otherwise convincing profile in Ireland last term and on UK debut on penulimate start. He can bounce back and play a big role

selections.comment: A very trappy affair with plenty in with a shout. Pietro and Brave Byreflection both arrive on the back of wins last time out and have scope for a bit more yet and are both solid options, with Pietro slightly more convicning given he's proven with cut in the ground. However, the one to take the eye most is GOLDEN REDEMPTION who made a very encouraging start to his UK career when a close-up third in a class 4 handicap at Newbury on first run since March. That was his first taste of turf having shown ability initially on dirt in Meydan before coming off the rails. He'll need to find a bit more but is in the hands of a a top trainer and a bold run is anticipated. Lever Up and U Sure Do are entitled to be thereabouts, while Green Persuit and Chesney's Charm could do better and have decent each way claims
